deep.reconstruction:
This page has no computation. It is a heavily reworked prose draft, in several successive attempts, of a passage in Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857). The passage belongs to the preliminary section 'Bestimmung einer Function einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse durch Grenz- und Unstetigkeitsbedingungen', which restates the Dirichlet-principle theorem of the 1851 dissertation (§§16–19).

Context from the adjacent pages:
- The previous page ends with a draft cover letter to the editor ('Euer Wohlgeboren', 'dritte Abhandlung', lectures of 1855 bis 1856). Above it is a constant count, ε = 2m' − p + 1, which is the Riemann(–Roch) count for functions with m' poles.
- The next page drafts the Riemann-surface section (a branched covering surface T, the exactness of X dx + Y dy, cross-cuts).
- So this sheet belongs to the preparation of the 1857 memoir.

Content, in modern terms:
(1) The 'Satz' referred to: on the cut, simply connected surface T', an analytic function w = u + iv can be determined with prescribed singularities ('Unstetigkeiten') in the interior and prescribed boundary behaviour. The underlying method is the Dirichlet principle: minimise Ω(α) = ∬_{T'} [(α_x − β_y)² + (α_y + β_x)²] dx dy over admissible α, with β a fixed comparison function.
(2) The restriction stated is the clean final version, which appears twice on the page: 'Für die Anwendung dieses Satzes ist der Umstand wichtig, dass eine Function von x+yi gewisse Unstetigkeiten, wie z. B. Unstetigkeiten erster Art, gar nicht annehmen kann.' Unstetigkeiten erster Art are jump discontinuities: a holomorphic or harmonic function cannot have them at interior points.
(3) The positive criterion follows: 'Eine Function von x+yi kann daher immer vorgeschriebenen Unstetigkeitsbedingungen gemäss bestimmt werden, wenn für jeden Punkt, wo sie unendlich werden soll, die vorgeschriebene Unstetigkeit die einer gegebenen dort unstetigen Function von x+yi ist.' In modern terms: a singularity can be prescribed at a point a whenever it is locally the principal part of some analytic function f_a, i.e. the target is w − f_a holomorphic near a. The struck lines give the reason, which is mine to make explicit: after subtracting such local models, the Dirichlet integral Ω(α) stays finite ('so bleibt Ω(α) endlich'), so the minimisation goes through. An arbitrary discontinuity, such as a jump, would make Ω infinite or be incompatible with harmonicity.
(4) The last lines start the boundary condition: the real part is to receive given values on the boundary ('reellen Theil in der Begrenzung … gegebenen Werth erhalten soll'). Implicitly the imaginary part is then determined up to an additive constant. The final fragment ('wesentliche Änderung …') is cut off.

Nothing is derived on the page. It is wording-work on the statement of the existence theorem.
errors: No mathematical error. The draft states the restriction loosely: 'gewisse Unstetigkeiten … gar nicht annehmen kann' is only made precise by the criterion that follows (the local singular behaviour must be that of an analytic function). This matches the published text.

The reliance on the Dirichlet principle (existence of a minimiser of Ω) is, by modern standards, unjustified as it stands (Weierstrass's objection, 1870; repaired by Hilbert, 1900/1904). This is the standard caveat, not a slip specific to this page.

results.what: Existence of an analytic function on a (cut) Riemann surface with prescribed singularities and prescribed real part on the boundary, via minimisation of the Dirichlet integral Ω(α)
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle / existence theorem for harmonic and meromorphic functions with prescribed singularities
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Dissertation 1851; Abelsche Functionen 1857); rigorous form by Hilbert

results.what: Admissible singularities are exactly those locally equal to the singularity of some analytic function; jump discontinuities (Unstetigkeiten erster Art) are impossible for analytic functions
results.modern_name: Local principal parts / Mittag-Leffler-type prescription of singularities; removability (no jump discontinuities of harmonic functions)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of a well-known passage of the published 1857 Abelian functions memoir (Dirichlet-principle preliminaries), with wording close to the printed text. It is of interest only for the genesis of the text, not for new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: x,y=symbols('x y',real=True); u=re(1/(x+I*y)).simplify(); v=im(1/(x+I*y)).simplify(); simplify(diff(u,x)-diff(v,y))==0 and simplify(diff(u,y)+diff(v,x))==0
checkable.asserts: A model singular function 1/(z−a) (here a=0) satisfies the Cauchy–Riemann equations away from its pole, so it is an admissible local singularity.
log|z| is harmonic away from 0, so it is an admissible logarithmic singularity of a real part.
The Dirichlet integral of log r diverges near the singularity. This is why the prescribed singular part must be subtracted first, keeping Ω(α) finite.
The constant count on the previous page, ε = 2m'−p+1, splits as m' + (m'−p+1), consistent with a Riemann–Roch-type count.

transcription_corrections: 'in Innern von T'' should read 'im Innern von T''.

The first clean sentence is better read as: 'Nach diesem Satze lässt sich eine Function von x+yi immer so bestimmen, dass sie im Innern von T' vorgeschriebene Unstetigkeiten annimmt …'. The interlinear 'zeigen' / 'nicht annehmen' belong to later revisions of this line.
'für jeden Punkt {+(gross[?])+} … unendlich werden sollen' is more likely 'für jeden Punkt, wo sie unendlich werden soll'; the bracketed 'gross' is doubtful.
'Unstetigkeitsklasse[?]' is probably 'Unstetigkeitsbedingungen' (cf. the clean line 'vorgeschriebenen Unstetigkeitsbedingungen gemäss bestimmt werden').

'durch[?] eine Function von x+yi gewisse Unstetigkeiten …' matches the published phrasing 'dass durch eine Function von x+yi gewisse Unstetigkeiten … nicht hervorgebracht werden können'. The draft here says 'gar nicht annehmen kann'.
